body.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\). Suppose the affirmative endpoint-response premise of the simultaneous margin-band theorem holds, and let \(C_0,C_1,n_0\) be the constants supplied there. After increasing \(n_0\) if necessary, for every \(n_\ast\ge n_0\), every \(p\ne q\), and every member of \(\mathcal M_s\), the following implication holds on \(\mathcal B_n\). If \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}+w_n<0\), then clipping at \(m/4\) is inactive and the distinct source-product trigger
\[
 \inf_{u\in\Omega}\lambda_{\min}\!\left(\operatorname{sym}\{\widehat H_p(u)\widehat H_q(u)\}\right)
 +(2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}<0
\]
holds. Given the validated oracle \(\mathcal O_n\), the exhaustive procedure in \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}negative\text{-}certificate}\) therefore terminates and returns \(\mathcal C_{pq,n}\ne\bot\). Its output contains rational \(u_0,z,t_{\mathrm{ch}}\), with \(z\ne0\) and \(u_0,u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z\in\operatorname{int}(\Omega)\), two outward-rounded interval enclosures containing the population increments \(F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_p(u_0)\) and \(F_q(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_q(u_0)\), and a rational upper bound strictly below zero for their inner product. Consequently,
\[
 \left\langle F_q(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_q(u_0),
 F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_p(u_0)\right\rangle<0,
\]
so \(C_{q\leftarrow p}\) is not Euclidean monotone on \(D_p\). The proposition does not assert that the source-product trigger and \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}+w_n<0\) are equivalent outside this eventual-radius regime.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 K:=\frac{2}{m}+\frac{2M}{m^2}=\frac{2(m+M)}{m^2},
 \qquad
 D_0:=\frac{4(m+M)}{m}+1,
 \qquad
 \overline r:=\frac{m}{2D_0}.
 \tag{1}
\]
These constants are positive because \(0<m<M\).  For every
\(0\le r\le\overline r\), expansion of the left-hand side gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K(m-r)^2-(2M+r)
 &=2m-D_0r+Kr^2\\
 &\ge 2m-D_0\overline r
 =\frac{3m}{2}>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
The affirmative endpoint-response premise in the proposition is used here only
to supply fixed constants \(C_0,C_1,n_0\); no probability assertion is used
below.  By the definitions of \(\ell_n\), \(h_n\), and
\(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}band}\),
\[
 r_{H,n}=C_1h_n^s
 =C_1\left\{\frac{\log(C_0Rn_\ast/\delta)}{n_\ast}\right\}^{s/(2s+d)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Here \(R<\infty\) by \(\mathrm{ass:regimes}\), \(\delta\) is fixed in
\((0,1/4)\), and \(s/(2s+d)>0\) by the declared ranges of \(s,d\) (in
particular, also by \(\mathrm{ass:smoothness\text{-}index}\)).  Since
\(\log(C_0Rn_\ast/\delta)/n_\ast\to0\), (3) tends to zero.  We may therefore
increase \(n_0\), without changing any assertion made for all
\(n_\ast\ge n_0\), so that
\[
 r:=r_{H,n}\le\overline r<\frac m2
 \qquad\text{whenever }n_\ast\ge n_0.
 \tag{4}
\]

Fix such an \(n_\ast\), an ordered pair \(p\ne q\), a member of
\(\mathcal M_s\), and a sample point in \(\mathcal B_n\).  Because (4) is the
radius premise of \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}margin\text{-}band}\), that
theorem and \(\mathrm{ass:hessian\text{-}ellipticity}\) imply, uniformly in
\(u\in\Omega\) and for \(a\in\{p,q\}\),
\[
 \widehat H_a(u)=\widetilde H_a(u),
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat H_a(u)-H_a(u)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le r,
 \qquad
 (m-r)I_d\preceq\widehat H_a(u)\preceq(M+r)I_d.
 \tag{5}
\]
In particular, clipping at \(m/4\) is inactive.  This explicitly restores the
eventual-radius premise before clipping inactivity is used.

We next compare the negative-margin endpoint with the different trigger used
by the certificate.  Define within this proof
\[
 \widehat S(u):=\operatorname{sym}\!\left(
   \widehat H_q(u)\widehat H_p(u)^{-1}\right),
 \qquad
 \widehat A(u):=\operatorname{sym}\!\left(
   \widehat H_p(u)\widehat H_q(u)\right).
 \tag{6}
\]
The fields in (6) are continuous by
\(\mathrm{def:regularized\text{-}hessian\text{-}estimator}\), and inversion
is continuous on the matrices bounded below in (5).  Since \(\Omega\) is
compact, the Rayleigh formula
\(\lambda_{\min}(G)=\min_{\lVert v\rVert_2=1}v^{\mathsf T}Gv\) shows that
\(u\mapsto\lambda_{\min}(\widehat S(u))\) is continuous and attains its
minimum.  Choose a minimizer \(u_\ast\) and a unit eigenvector \(v_\ast\)
corresponding to its smallest eigenvalue.  Symmetry of the two Hessian fields
gives the exact congruence identity
\[
 \widehat A(u)=\widehat H_p(u)\widehat S(u)\widehat H_p(u).
 \tag{7}
\]
With \(z_\ast:=\widehat H_p(u_\ast)^{-1}v_\ast\), equations (5)--(7) yield
\[
 z_\ast^{\mathsf T}\widehat A(u_\ast)z_\ast
 =v_\ast^{\mathsf T}\widehat S(u_\ast)v_\ast
 =\widehat\gamma_{pq},
 \qquad
 0<\lVert z_\ast\rVert_2\le(m-r)^{-1}.
 \tag{8}
\]
If \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}+w_n<0\), then
\(\widehat\gamma_{pq}<-Kr<0\), because
\(w_n=Kr\) by \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}band}\).  Applying the
Rayleigh formula to \(\widehat A(u_\ast)\), and observing that the negative
number \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\) reverses the useful direction when it is
multiplied by
\(\lVert z_\ast\rVert_2^{-2}\ge(m-r)^2\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \inf_{u\in\Omega}\lambda_{\min}(\widehat A(u))
 &\le \lambda_{\min}(\widehat A(u_\ast))\\
 &\le
 \frac{z_\ast^{\mathsf T}\widehat A(u_\ast)z_\ast}
      {\lVert z_\ast\rVert_2^2}\\
 &\le(m-r)^2\widehat\gamma_{pq}\\
 &<-K(m-r)^2r\\
 &<-(2M+r)r,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
where the last inequality is (2).  Thus
\[
 \inf_{u\in\Omega}\lambda_{\min}\!\left(
 \operatorname{sym}\{\widehat H_p(u)\widehat H_q(u)\}\right)
 +(2M+r)r<0.
 \tag{10}
\]
Equation (9) is a one-way implication; no equivalence between the margin
trigger and the source-product trigger has been used or asserted.

We now prove finite termination of the construction.  The expression
\[
 (u,z)\longmapsto
 z^{\mathsf T}\widehat A(u)z+(2M+r)r\lVert z\rVert_2^2
 \tag{11}
\]
is continuous.  From (10), the Rayleigh formula supplies a point and a
nonzero direction at which (11) is negative.  The interior of the closed unit
ball is dense in \(\Omega\), rational interior points are dense there, and
\(\mathbb Q^d\setminus\{0\}\) is dense in
\(\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\).  Strictness and continuity of (11) therefore
give
\[
 u_0\in\operatorname{int}(\Omega)\cap\mathbb Q^d,
 \qquad z\in\mathbb Q^d\setminus\{0\},
 \tag{12}
\]
such that
\[
 z^{\mathsf T}\widehat A(u_0)z
 +(2M+r)r\lVert z\rVert_2^2<0.
 \tag{13}
\]
For all sufficiently small \(t>0\), the compact chord
\(u_0+[0,t]z\) is contained in \(\operatorname{int}(\Omega)\).  On such a
chord set
\[
 \widehat a(t):=\int_0^t\widehat H_p(u_0+\tau z)z\,d\tau,
 \qquad
 \widehat b(t):=\int_0^t\widehat H_q(u_0+\tau z)z\,d\tau.
 \tag{14}
\]
Continuity of the Hessian fields implies
\[
 t^{-1}\widehat a(t)\longrightarrow\widehat H_p(u_0)z,
 \qquad
 t^{-1}\widehat b(t)\longrightarrow\widehat H_q(u_0)z
 \quad(t\downarrow0).
 \tag{15}
\]
For a scalar quadratic form, a matrix may be replaced by its symmetric part;
hence (15) and (6) give
\[
 \lim_{t\downarrow0}t^{-2}
 \langle\widehat b(t),\widehat a(t)\rangle
 =z^{\mathsf T}\widehat H_q(u_0)\widehat H_p(u_0)z
 =z^{\mathsf T}\widehat A(u_0)z.
 \tag{16}
\]
By (13), (16), and density of \(\mathbb Q_{>0}\), there is a rational
\(t_{\mathrm{ch}}>0\) for which both chord endpoints are interior and
\[
 \langle\widehat b(t_{\mathrm{ch}}),
          \widehat a(t_{\mathrm{ch}})\rangle
 +(2M+r)r t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2<0.
 \tag{17}
\]

Apply the validated range oracle from
\(\mathrm{def:validated\text{-}range\text{-}oracle}\) to rational boxes
covering successive rational subdivisions of this chord.  Multiplication of
each interval matrix by \(z\), followed by multiplication by the rational
segment length and interval addition, encloses each vector integral in (14).
The excess diameter of the oracle intervals tends to zero by that definition;
the actual range diameter on each segment also tends to zero by uniform
continuity of the clipped fields on the compact chord.  Consequently the two
vector enclosures shrink to the integrals in (14).  Continuity of the
finite-dimensional scalar product then shows that their outward-rounded upper
endpoints \(U_J\) satisfy
\[
 U_J\longrightarrow
 \langle\widehat b(t_{\mathrm{ch}}),
          \widehat a(t_{\mathrm{ch}})\rangle
 \quad(J\to\infty).
 \tag{18}
\]
It follows from the strict inequality (17) that a finite refinement level
\(J\) satisfies
\[
 U_J+(2M+r)r t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2<0.
 \tag{19}
\]
As specified in
\(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}negative\text{-}certificate}\), outward rational
rounding returns a negative rational upper endpoint once (19) holds.  The
enumeration is exhaustive, so the finite-height rational triple in
(12)--(17) is eventually examined and refined through level \(J\).  The
procedure therefore terminates and returns
\(\mathcal C_{pq,n}\ne\bot\).

It remains to prove population validity.  By
\(\mathrm{ass:potential\text{-}holder}\), the maps
\(F_a=\nabla\varphi_a\) are continuously differentiable on the chord, with
derivatives \(H_a\).  The fundamental theorem of calculus therefore gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 a_0&:=F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_p(u_0)
 =\int_0^{t_{\mathrm{ch}}}H_p(u_0+\tau z)z\,d\tau,\\
 b_0&:=F_q(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_q(u_0)
 =\int_0^{t_{\mathrm{ch}}}H_q(u_0+\tau z)z\,d\tau.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{20}
\]
The error bound in (5), integrated along the chord, yields
\[
 \lVert a_0-\widehat a(t_{\mathrm{ch}})\rVert_2
 \le rt_{\mathrm{ch}}\lVert z\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 \lVert b_0-\widehat b(t_{\mathrm{ch}})\rVert_2
 \le rt_{\mathrm{ch}}\lVert z\rVert_2.
 \tag{21}
\]
Every coordinate error is bounded by its Euclidean norm, so the coordinatewise
enlargements prescribed in
\(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}negative\text{-}certificate}\) contain the two
population increments in (20).  Furthermore,
\(H_p\preceq MI_d\) by \(\mathrm{ass:hessian\text{-}ellipticity}\), while
\(\widehat H_q\preceq(M+r)I_d\) by (5).  Hence
\[
 \lVert a_0\rVert_2\le Mt_{\mathrm{ch}}\lVert z\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat b(t_{\mathrm{ch}})\rVert_2
 \le(M+r)t_{\mathrm{ch}}\lVert z\rVert_2.
 \tag{22}
\]
Using the exact identity
\[
 \langle b_0,a_0\rangle-
 \langle\widehat b,\widehat a\rangle
 =\langle b_0-\widehat b,a_0\rangle
  +\langle\widehat b,a_0-\widehat a\rangle
\]
at \(t=t_{\mathrm{ch}}\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz and (21)--(22), gives
\[
 \left|\langle b_0,a_0\rangle-
 \langle\widehat b(t_{\mathrm{ch}}),
          \widehat a(t_{\mathrm{ch}})\rangle\right|
 \le(2M+r)r t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2.
 \tag{23}
\]
Thus the scalar allowance in the certificate is valid, and (19) supplies a
strict negative rational upper bound for \(\langle b_0,a_0\rangle\).  In
particular,
\[
 \left\langle F_q(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_q(u_0),
 F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)-F_p(u_0)\right\rangle<0.
 \tag{24}
\]

Finally, \(t_{\mathrm{ch}}z\ne0\), and the lower ellipticity bound gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle a_0,t_{\mathrm{ch}}z\rangle
 &=\int_0^{t_{\mathrm{ch}}}
 t_{\mathrm{ch}}z^{\mathsf T}H_p(u_0+\tau z)z\,d\tau\\
 &\ge m t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{25}
\]
Therefore \(x_0:=F_p(u_0)\) and
\(x_1:=F_p(u_0+t_{\mathrm{ch}}z)\) are distinct points of \(D_p\).
Definition \(\mathrm{def:counterfactual\text{-}map}\), whose causal
interpretation is supplied by \(\mathrm{ass:shared\text{-}rank\text{-}scm}\),
gives
\[
 C_{q\leftarrow p}(F_p(u))=F_q(u).
 \tag{26}
\]
A map \(T\) is Euclidean monotone precisely when
\(\langle T(x_1)-T(x_0),x_1-x_0\rangle\ge0\) for every pair in its domain.
Applying (26) at the two chord endpoints makes the left-hand side of this
inequality equal to the quantity in (24), which is strictly negative.
Therefore \(C_{q\leftarrow p}\) is not Euclidean monotone on \(D_p\), as
claimed.
body.justification: The proposition proves that, beyond an explicit eventual-radius threshold supplied by the simultaneous band, a negative margin-band endpoint quantitatively forces the distinct source-product trigger and yields a reproducible rational violating chord with validated population enclosures.
body.gap: The located Brenier estimation and multivariate-rank papers provide norm bounds or scalar tests, not a terminating interval certificate whose distinct source-product trigger is rigorously linked to the statistical margin endpoint in the eventual-radius regime.
body.consumer: Model auditors retain the scalar margin test and, when its negative endpoint occurs beyond the certified radius threshold, additionally receive rational source points, validated population-increment enclosures, and a strict sign witness.
